title: One Unified SLM · Training Progress
motivation: Three separate SLM workloads (MAI Profile, Quality, GEM story-assembly) each carried their own small fine-tune. The initiative consolidates them into ONE joint model fine-tuned over a merged train set, so all workloads share one served model and one inference footprint.
Start small (~4B Qwen3) to prove the orchestration end-to-end; the joint SFT can later be swapped to a larger MoE base if Quality/HPF capacity becomes the gating factor.

The AML A100 pool hands every job exactly ONE GPU (confirmed via gpu_diag). To use the fleet's GPUs at once, the train set is split into K disjoint shards, each trained on one node, then recombined by weight-delta averaging (model soup):  final = base + mean_k(shard_k − base).
dataset: Train = MAI Profile (L1 70,952 + L2 74,327 rows) merged with Quality clickbait (10,646 rows) and GEM story-assembly (~150k rows recovered from Kusto GSPEventJob StorylineLog, 2026-09-19→10-11) → one joint SFT set.
data_prepare merges each task's train.jsonl under one_unified_slm/<run>/data/train.jsonl (per-shard slice ≈ 35.9k rows at K=4).
Each example keeps its natural chat structure (role/turn threads); layer_format generic; max_seq_len 8192 truncates the tail.
joint train split deterministically by seed 42 into K disjoint shards; each shard job slices its own lines on-node, no data re-upload.

summary: Pipeline: data_synth → data_prepare → sft → eval · Sharded single-GPU SFT over a 1-GPU-per-job A100 pool, merged by weight-delta averaging. Root cause of r1–r8 failures: multi-GPU --num_processes 8 on a 1-GPU pool (invalid device ordinal). K=1 smoke proved the on-node slice + single-GPU render; fixed an eval-time CUDA OOM by disabling eval during shard training.
